transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time. 

I guess I came in because... well, I haven't been feeling quite like myself lately. It probably sounds silly, and I'm sure you see people with much worse problems, but most days I just feel like I'm sitting at the bottom of this really dark hole. I try really hard to put on a good face, you know, not let it bother anyone else. But even when I'm around people I know well, I just can't seem to shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds a bit dramatic. Is that... is that the kind of thing you need to know? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
How long have you been feeling this heavy, hopeless feeling?

Well, um... I guess it's been a little while now. I really tried to just push through it, you know, to not let it get the best of me. But... it's been about a year and two months, I think? 

It all kind of started after I had this fall at work—I do HVAC repair—and I ended up with a back injury. After that, it just felt like... well, like everything sort of started unraveling on me. I'm sorry, I hope I'm not complaining too much, or making a bigger deal out of a work accident than I should. Does that... does that timeline help you at all?
Do you still find pleasure in activities that you used to enjoy?

Well, um... I guess I've been a little less active lately. I used to really love doing things, you know? Like hiking, or painting... I even liked going down to the local makerspace to tinker with things. And honestly, even figuring out a really tricky HVAC install used to give me a lot of satisfaction. 

But lately... I don't know, it's probably just me being lazy, but I just end up staring at my painting supplies or my tools, and it just doesn't feel worth starting. I've even been ignoring calls from friends who want to go hiking or meet up. I feel terrible about it, I really do. I know I should just force myself to go out and do things, and I'm probably making it sound worse than it is. I just... I can't seem to find the energy or the interest I used to have. 

I'm sorry, is that the kind of answer you were looking for? I hope I'm not sounding too negative.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately?

Well, um... my sleep has been a little off, I suppose. I don't want to make it sound like a huge deal, because I know everyone has trouble sleeping sometimes. But... I guess it's been pretty erratic. 

Sometimes I just lie awake for hours. My back will be hurting from the accident, and my mind just races with, you know, worrying about bills and everything. And then other times... well, I feel so guilty about this, but I'll end up sleeping for half the day. And the worst part is, even when I do that, I still wake up feeling like I haven't rested at all. 

I'm probably just not managing my schedule very well, and I know I should try harder to get on a normal routine. I hope that makes sense? I'm sorry if I'm rambling too much about it.
Have you had any thoughts about hurting yourself or ending your life?

Well, um... I guess... I mean, I know a lot of people probably get overwhelmed sometimes, right? I don't want you to think I'm crazy or anything, or that I'm, you know, a danger. I really try to keep a positive attitude most days. 

But... sometimes, when my back is just throbbing and the bills are sitting there on the counter... I have had these thoughts. Just... thinking that maybe it would be easier for everyone if I just didn't wake up. Like I'm just a burden right now. And, well, I guess a few times I've caught myself actually thinking about... about ending it. 

It really scares me when my mind goes there, I promise I don't want to do anything like that. I feel so ashamed even admitting it out loud. I know I should be stronger than that. I'm sorry, I hope that's not too alarming... is it okay that I told you that?
Have you noticed any changes in your movement or activity level, such as feeling restless or sluggish?

Well, um... I guess I have been a little slower lately. I mean, I don't want to make a big deal out of it, because I know my back injury probably slows me down some, and everyone gets tired, right? 

But... honestly, it feels like everything I do just takes so much effort now. Like, even just getting up from the couch to go to the kitchen feels like I'm moving through molasses. And it's not just my body, either. Sometimes my husband or my kids will ask me a simple question, and it just... it takes me a minute to even process it and answer. 

People keep asking me if I'm okay because they say I'm moving like I'm underwater. I feel really bad about it, like I'm frustrating everyone around me by being so sluggish. I try to speed up, I really do, but my body just won't cooperate. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's the kind of information you need? I know I probably just need to push myself a little harder to get moving.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Well, um... I guess my eating habits have been a little, you know, all over the place lately. I mean, I really try to eat right, I know how important nutrition is, especially when you're trying to heal. I don't want you to think I'm just completely letting myself go.

But... well, during the day, I just can't seem to force anything down. Food just kind of turns my stomach right now, so I end up running on just coffee for most of the day. And then, I feel so silly admitting this, but late at night, I'll just stand there and pick at whatever is in the cabinet. I'm not even really tasting it, you know? It's just... mindless, I guess. 

I haven't weighed myself because I'm a little afraid to look, but I'm sure my clothes are fitting a bit differently. I know I should be making better meals for myself, and I really am going to try to do better with that. I hope it's okay that I'm just eating like that right now? I'm sorry, I know it's not very healthy.
Do you often feel guilty about things that have happened in your life?

Well, um... I guess everyone has regrets, right? I try really hard to focus on the future and not dwell on the past. I know that's what you're supposed to do, and I don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself all day. 

But... lately, it's just been really hard to shut my brain off. With my back being like this, I can't do my job anymore, and... I just keep telling myself how useless I am now. I sit here and I just replay things over and over. Like, every apprentice I ever let down at work, or every bill sitting on the counter that I can't pay right now. 

It just feels like... like all of it is proof that I've just ruined everything for my family. I feel so guilty that I can't provide the way I used to, and I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself. I really am trying to look on the bright side, I promise. I hope it doesn't make me sound terrible, admitting all that... is it normal to feel this bad about things?
Have you been feeling fidgety or having an intense need to move around?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, I know some people get really anxious and pace around or tap their feet a lot when they're stressed, and I guess it's good that I don't do that, right? I try to stay calm and not be a bother to anyone. 

Honestly, it's kind of the opposite for me right now. Like I was saying before, it's just so hard to get moving at all. I don't really have that... that urge to jump up and do things. I kind of wish I did, maybe then I could get more done around the house and be more helpful. 

But no, I haven't been feeling fidgety or anything like that. I hope that's an okay answer? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you experienced any strange or unusual thoughts, like hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there?

Well, um... no. No, nothing like that. I mean, I know things are pretty messy in my head right now with all the worrying and the guilt, but I'm definitely not... you know, I'm not losing touch with reality or anything. I really try hard to stay grounded, even when I'm feeling this low. 

I haven't heard any voices or seen anything strange at all. I hope you don't think I'm... well, crazy, just because I've been struggling so much lately to keep it together. It's a good sign that I'm not experiencing those kinds of things, right? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers... I hope it's a good thing that I don't have that happening.
Have you had any periods in the last two weeks where you felt significantly better for a few days?

Well, um... I really wish I could tell you yes. I know I'm supposed to be, you know, trying to pull myself up and have good days. And I really do try to put on a brave face for my family so I'm not bringing everyone down all the time. 

But if I'm being completely honest... no, not really. The last couple of weeks have just been... well, kind of a flat line, I guess. I haven't really had a stretch where I felt significantly better. 

I hope that's not disappointing to hear. I really am trying my best to snap out of it, I promise. It's just been so hard to shake this heavy feeling off. Is it... is it okay that I haven't had a good few days yet? I just want to make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to be doing to get better.
Have you had any periods where you felt nearly back to normal, even if only for a brief moment, in the past two weeks?

Well, um... I guess maybe just for a second here or there? Like, if I'm at work—I do repair work, so I have to focus on fixing things—sometimes I'll get distracted for just a minute while I'm figuring out a problem. And maybe in that one little moment, I don't feel quite as... heavy. 

But it doesn't really last. It's not like I feel totally normal again, even though I really, really wish I did. I try to hold onto those little moments so I can do a good job and not let my boss down. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the answer you're looking for. I wish I could say I was feeling back to myself more often. Is it... is it normal that it hasn't really happened yet? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are going.
Are there any activities that you still enjoy or find pleasure in?

Well, um... I really try to keep busy, you know? I don't want to just sit around and mope. I used to be really active—I loved hiking, and painting, and I'd spend hours tinkering with stuff at the local makerspace. Even at work, figuring out a really tricky install used to be something I actually looked forward to. 

But lately... I don't know, I guess I've been a little less involved. I tell myself I'm just tired, but... honestly, I'll just sit and stare at my painting supplies, or I'll ignore calls from my friends about going to the makerspace. It just... it doesn't feel worth the effort to even start. 

I feel terrible admitting that. I know I should be forcing myself to do things I used to like, and I really am trying to find the motivation. It's just so hard right now. Does that make sense? I hope you don't think I'm just being lazy... I really want to enjoy those things again, I promise.
Are there any small things that still bring you joy or make you happy?

Oh... um, I'm sorry, I feel like I'm just being a broken record and being so negative. I really wish I could give you a more positive answer, I truly do. I know you're just looking for one little thing we can build on. 

But, like I was just saying a minute ago about the painting and the makerspace... I used to love all of that so much. You'd think even just doing a tiny sketch, or a really small fix on an install at work, or even a short walk instead of a long hike would bring a little spark back. But... it just doesn't right now. I still just stare at my supplies, or I let the phone ring when people call to invite me out, because even the smallest piece of it just doesn't feel worth the energy to start. 

I feel awful saying that out loud to you. I really want to be making progress and finding those little joys. I hope you're not frustrated with me... I'm answering your questions okay, aren't I? I just don't want you to think I'm not trying.
Are you able to experience pleasure when you do things that you normally enjoy?

I... I know we were just talking about this, and I'm really sorry to keep saying the same thing. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or difficult to work with. I just... I want to make sure I'm answering you right. 

When I try to do those things I normally enjoy, like... like I said, the painting or the makerspace, or even a hike... I don't really feel that spark anymore. I'll just kind of sit there looking at my paints, or I'll see my phone buzzing with a text from a friend wanting to go do something, and I just... I ignore it. It just feels like too much effort to even begin, and the good feeling I used to get just isn't there right now. 

I'm really trying, though. I know I need to push myself more. Is that... is that okay to admit? I just don't want you to think I've given up.
Have you experienced any significant improvement in your mood or symptoms over the past two weeks?

I... gosh, I really wish I could give you a better answer. I've been trying so hard to have a good week so I could come in here and tell you things were looking up. But... if I'm being completely honest, it's just been more of the same. I haven't really felt any kind of lift or improvement lately. 

I'm so sorry, I hate coming in here and just being a raincloud every time. I feel like I'm letting you down by not bouncing back faster. I really am trying my best to push through it, I promise. Is it... is it okay that it's taking this long? I just want to make sure I'm not failing at this, or frustrating you by not getting better yet.
Are you able to feel pleasure or enjoyment when something good happens to you?

I... oh, I feel so terrible having to give you the same kind of answer again. I really hope you don't think I'm just being stubborn or refusing to see the bright side. I want to be able to tell you yes, absolutely, I feel so happy when good things happen. 

But... even when something objectively good happens, like... say I finally figure out a really tricky install at work. That used to feel so good, you know? I'd be so proud of myself. Or if someone calls with a fun invite to go hiking, or to go tinkering at the makerspace... I just don't get that happy feeling from it anymore. I know I keep bringing up the same examples, but it's true... I still just end up staring at my painting supplies, or ignoring those calls from people, because even the good things just don't feel worth the energy of starting or engaging with. 

I'm so sorry. I feel like such a broken record today. I promise I'm trying to appreciate the good moments when they happen... am I doing this wrong? I just really want to be getting better for you, and I hate feeling like I'm not giving you the right answers.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt completely back to normal?

I... I really wish I could say yes. I've been trying so hard to get back to normal, and I'm so sorry to keep giving you bad news. I know I should be doing better, and I hate feeling like I'm disappointing you. 

But... no, I haven't really had a normal day lately. Actually, that's kind of the main reason I finally came in to see you. I don't want to sound dramatic—I know other people have it so much worse—but most days lately, I just feel like I'm sitting at the bottom of a really dark hole. And even when I try to push through it, like when I'm around people I know and I'm trying to just smile and be normal... I just can't seem to shake this really heavy, hopeless feeling. 

I'm trying so hard to snap out of it, I promise I am. Is it... is it okay that I feel that way? I just hope I'm explaining it right, and I really hope you don't think I'm just feeling sorry for myself.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt even slightly better than the others?

I... gosh, I keep racking my brain trying to find just one day to give you. Just a morning, even, where things felt a little lighter so I could tell you about it. But... honestly, it's all just been this one long, heavy blur. I haven't really noticed any shift from one day to the next. 

I feel awful being so negative all the time. I really don't want you to think I'm not trying, because I wake up every morning hoping today will be the day I can finally come in here and say, 'Yes, Tuesday was a better day!' But... it just hasn't happened yet. 

Is it... is it normal for it to just stay this flat for so long? I'm so sorry, I just really hope I'm not being a difficult patient for you to help. I promise I'm doing my best to find the bright spots.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt even slightly better than the others, but still not completely back to normal?

I... oh, I know you just asked me that, and I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm giving you the exact same answer again. I really don't mean to be difficult or repetitive. I want so badly to give you a different answer, to say that yes, maybe yesterday afternoon was a little bit better, or that I felt a tiny bit lighter on Sunday. 

But... it's just like I was saying before. It's just this constant feeling of being at the bottom of that dark hole. It doesn't really lift, even a little bit. Even when I'm trying my hardest to put on a brave face around my friends or family, that heavy, hopeless feeling is just... it's just always there, weighing me down. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's not what you want to hear. I really am trying to notice if things get even a little bit better. Am I... is it okay that I don't have a better day to tell you about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so you can help me.

patient.answer:
Well, um... I guess everyone has regrets, right? I try really hard to focus on the future and not dwell on the past. I know that's what you're supposed to do, and I don't want to sound like I'm just sitting around feeling sorry for myself all day. 

But... lately, it's just been really hard to shut my brain off. With my back being like this, I can't do my job anymore, and... I just keep telling myself how useless I am now. I sit here and I just replay things over and over. Like, every apprentice I ever let down at work, or every bill sitting on the counter that I can't pay right now. 

It just feels like... like all of it is proof that I've just ruined everything for my family. I feel so guilty that I can't provide the way I used to, and I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself. I really am trying to look on the bright side, I promise. I hope it doesn't make me sound terrible, admitting all that... is it normal to feel this bad about things?
